options.content:
3. Provider Health / GLOBAL

Current window: provider status from fixed recording-rule windows. Selected provider: $provider. Pipeline context: $pipeline_context.

panels.description: Provider severity mapping: 0=OK, 1=DEGRADED, 2=FAILING; null/NaN=UNKNOWN. Raw provider health status remains panel id=114 with 0=UNHEALTHY, 1=DEGRADED, 2=HEALTHY. This matrix intentionally stays GLOBAL and does not filter by pipeline.
panels.title: Monitor GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix

panels.description: Only providers currently DEGRADED or FAILING. Empty table means no provider currently above OK; providers with missing current-status telemetry remain visible as UNKNOWN in the GLOBAL severity matrix.
panels.title: Inspect Critical Providers

panels.description: Current top provider causes from canonical cause recording rules: raw status, failure rate, retry exhaustion, latency, HTTP errors, or rate-limit pressure. Empty table means no active provider causes are currently above zero.
panels.title: Inspect Provider Top Causes

options.content: First action: start with the GLOBAL severity matrix, then open top causes for the degraded provider. If cause is retry/rate-limit/circuit-breaker, inspect control-plane safety before replay. If cause is latency/errors, correlate with Runtime impact, then logs/traces from the runtime or DQ dashboards.

panels.title: Track Health Check Latency by Provider (p95)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: p95 provider health-check latency over the active Grafana interval. Current provider severity is owned by the GLOBAL Provider Severity Matrix.

panels.title: Monitor Current Provider Health Status
panels.description: Provider raw enum: 0=UNHEALTHY, 1=DEGRADED, 2=HEALTHY; null/NaN=UNKNOWN when the provider exists but raw status is absent. First-screen severity uses bioetl_provider_current_status to avoid inverting raw enum colors.

panels.title: Monitor Healthy Checks (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: completed HEALTHY probes in the active Grafana range. This panel is not a current-health source.

targets.expr: (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) / clamp_min((sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_success_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_degraded_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: Track Provider Failure Rate (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: failed probes divided by completed probes in the active Grafana range. Current status comes from bioetl_provider_current_status. Gauge thresholds follow the provider policy contract: warning at 5%, critical at 20%.

targets.expr: round((sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_success_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_degraded_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)) + (sum(increase(bioetl_health_check_failures_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__range])) or vector(0)))

panels.title: Track Health Checks Total (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: total completed provider health checks in the active Grafana range.

panels.title: Monitor Degraded Checks (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: completed DEGRADED probes in the active Grafana range. This panel is not a current-health source, so non-zero counts remain neutral evidence rather than WARN/CRIT by themselves.

panels.title: Track Failure and Degraded Trend by Provider
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: failure/degraded probe trend over the active Grafana interval.

panels.title: Track Provider Failure Share (Selected Range)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: provider share of failed probes in the active Grafana range.

panels.title: Track Retries Exhausted by Provider/Operation
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: retries exhausted by provider and operation in the active Grafana range. Non-zero rows identify where retry budgets were consumed, not raw provider-health enum state.

panels.title: Track Retries Exhausted Trend by Provider/Operation
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: retry exhaustion trend by provider and operation over the active Grafana interval. Rising non-zero series point to persistent retry-budget pressure.
Expand only after selecting one provider or a bounded provider subset.
panels.title: Selected Provider Detail
Inspect Provider Health Check Latency (p95) - $provider
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: per-provider p95 health-check latency over the active Grafana range. No data means no latency samples or no probe activity in range, not 0s latency.

panels.title: Inspect Adapter Request Latency by Endpoint (p95)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: p95 adapter request latency by endpoint for the selected provider scope. No data remains diagnostic and means no endpoint latency samples in range. The provider degraded-rule surface fires at p95 > 5s; lower bands here are earlier-warning inspect thresholds.

targets.expr: round(sum by (provider, method, error_type) (increase(bioetl_http_request_errors_total{provider=~"$provider"}[$__interval])) or vector(0))

panels.title: Inspect HTTP Errors by Method/Error Type
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: HTTP error volume grouped by provider, method, and error_type for the active Grafana interval.

panels.title: Track Rate Limiter Wait by Provider (p95)
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: p95 wait time imposed by provider rate limiting. No data means no observed wait samples in range. The provider degraded-rule surface starts at p95 > 1s; this panel keeps a lower yellow band for earlier-warning inspection.

panels.title: Monitor Minimum Rate Limiter Tokens Available
panels.description: Selected-range evidence: minimum provider tokens available in the active Grafana range. Lower values indicate higher rate-limit pressure; 0 means requests can be blocked. No data remains diagnostic and means no token samples were observed in range.

panels.title: Monitor Cross-Scope Adapter Circuit Breaker State (max)
panels.description: Cross-scope adapter diagnostics over the active Grafana range: 0=CLOSED, 1=HALF_OPEN, 2=OPEN. Uses the adapter selector because the shipped metric family is adapter-labelled rather than provider-labelled. No data remains diagnostic and does not imply a synthetic CLOSED state.

panels.title: Track Cross-Scope Adapter Circuit Breaker Trips
panels.description: Cross-scope adapter diagnostics: selected-range circuit-breaker trip count by adapter over the active Grafana interval. This panel is intentionally adapter-scoped because the shipped metric family is adapter-labelled rather than provider-labelled. No data remains diagnostic and does not create synthetic adapter rows.
